These are the machine\'s own figures. A night runs from midday to midday and has the date of the evening. Its figures arrive after it has ended. Times are corrected to the phone\'s clock. AHI is the number of apnoeas and hypopnoeas for each hour of use. Median means that the value was below this figure for half of the time in use. A column such as 5%, 70% or 95% means that the value was at or below this figure for that share of the time in use. Max is the highest value. A dash (—) means that the machine recorded no value.

The machine records each event with a time. For an apnoea with a length, this is the time it ended. The machine records no length for a hypopnoea. Its time can be its start or its end. Times are corrected to the phone\'s clock. A time with * is by the machine\'s clock, because PAPRelay could not correct it. Nights without events are not listed.

resources.string: Usage, AHI, leak, pressure and breathing for each night are written to the health records in Health Connect. They appear there under lab results, from “PAPRelay (CPAP machine)”. They are not laboratory results.

Google Health shows these records only with a name and a date of birth. PAPRelay writes them only to this phone and to Health Connect. Apps that you allow to read health records, such as Google Health, can then read them.

Respiratory rate starts after a night of therapy of one hour or more. First PAPRelay checks that it reads the data of this machine\'s software version correctly. If it has not started after a few nights, switch it off in Sharing.
One value for each minute of therapy. Leave this off if another device already writes your respiratory rate.

Two files, kept up to date in a folder that you choose. paprelay_nights.csv has one line for each night. paprelay_events.csv has one line for each breathing event. If the folder is on a cloud drive, other programs can read the files there. PAPRelay itself sends nothing: it hands the files to the folder.

The device check reads from the machine and changes none of its settings or data. Pairing replaces the myAir app\'s connection to the machine. For each thing that is switched on in Sharing, the check writes a made-up test entry to Health Connect and removes it again. An empty source named “PAPRelay (CPAP machine)” stays in the health records.

What PAPRelay does with your data

PAPRelay reads therapy records from your machine over Bluetooth and stores them on this phone. If you leave it switched on, it writes each night\'s figures to the health records in Health Connect. If you switch it on, it writes respiratory rate to Health Connect. If you choose a folder, it keeps two files of nights and breathing events there. It does this when you ask, and from time to time in the background when the machine is in range.

Your data goes nowhere else. PAPRelay has no internet permission, no accounts, no analytics and no advertising. Data leaves the app only through Health Connect, through the files in a folder that you choose, through a report that you save, and when you share it with another app yourself.
What PAPRelay reads from Health Connect
PAPRelay reads nothing from Health Connect. It asks only for permission to write.

Uninstalling PAPRelay deletes everything it stored itself. The files kept in a folder that you chose stay there until you delete them. Records it wrote to Health Connect can be removed in Health Connect.
